أن برقـلهما بتأو مليب فلاسعو مع مسلم من ذلك وصما الما كلا المله
فلا فتاله إن إذا الخالطات الأرضيه بما يسهل يهما بها عن اليقين والجهوم لما لكلك
له ولا لذتها وده ولا ومنهل ريس بها من الكنف فكانب ملله والطخو
مسدد ماجه ور والطيرن المح الما المز الما الساه له أما المطره
خصوصا ساما كا وصصفا أن من حيث كأمد والدا الذي كن من حاب جي بلح
عاسم هـ فيكون كذا لكنا الذا بالكذي وكوالمثا لك يتالى أرتبع سطم ظه
سكن شسبر للجيم عب سبا الذاار المغوبه با أدا ذلك ما ما ذلك يأء المطرب ران
كالفضل وا للكون بلا ان لأنه من يه نفوره فيه المسد الأبهق والهواك
سرعه ويضر بعضها عضبا بالاطلاط إسلو السلين الأطلاط والصد دها والصيا لصا ل
قو رالكتب في ذلك لك ثلاك ان ما سوء هادها من طيا أنه طيأ تخفية ولو كأن
البت سدذ البت ذالك لكان ما كانب المطلب ما كان ما عنب ثمجود دالبس وكذلك وكله لمده
translation:
(Right page)
Concerning earthy waters of little purity — Ibn Hayyan has noted that their excess renders them unsuitable. The balanced measure requires that the water be purified and clarified, for corruption of its mixture occurs when the refining of the water is left incomplete. When the earthy parts enter deeply into the water without proper settling and filtering, and the condition remains as described, then the excess of those mixed parts within it causes harm. The water should be purified so that each part may fully clarify. When the water is thoroughly freed from its admixtures, it enters into a state of refinement; the greatest virtue being that it becomes like rain-water or something close to it in lightness and purity. The thick water should be treated by compounding and mixing, and its heaviness corrected through proper means. When the thick water is composed from such sources and then boiled gently and made into the lightest and finest water, it becomes suitable. The water obtained from grapevines — whether thin or the refined product of the distilled raisin-infusion — clarifies well. Its turbidity settles after some time in seasons like those of Sirin, and when it is purified, its color changes and becomes saline in quality.

(Left page)
As for the Nile when it overflows its banks — travellers and scholars have gathered information about it over many years from those who know its country. The water flows to the lowlands, flooding broadly and spreading widely, and within it are mixed substances. The sediment settles from it little by little, and every part clarifies over time, so one should not disturb it, for it purifies itself remarkably. If one takes it mixed with earthy materials, it is made easy to treat by what is known of purification methods based on experience and sound reasoning. It has no great pleasure nor does it lead to harm when taken carefully, as long as the turbid and earthy mixing agents are removed. The river water — especially the Nile — is characterized by particular qualities owing to the nature of its source and the long distance it travels over beneficial and gentle terrain. Thus it settles and clarifies, each part balancing the other through dispersion and movement. The mixing of its properties and the speed of their mutual action, combined with settling of its heavy impurities, makes it — as the books have recorded — among the best waters when it has completed its course, having been purified by time and by nature, free of sediment, and its use sustained over long periods.

text:
Right page:

لطافة منه فان كل طيف الجوهر فوامه قابل للأفعال وإذا اورد الى
ما الطلق اقل علو المعقوله والحوضات إذا كانت موجثم وفيم الضرور
ه الشيء اسطغابل للقفو منه من كل ما اذا اردنا لطف ما الباب
الى بناء البيوت وديبه وذلك لاتصابه محمد به مخالطه للأضبات
مثله لطيله لاخلال اعى يمنعنى ادل الستحك بيمه ماس لامن فيها
ما اذ الحال لطهور والأضنام بل الجبله والصناعه اى ان قب له الاسبل
الحل لبتصح ما ما مجسل ماء الأكثر ماء للكثف المثمانين بمنعنى فيه وبعقع
كبيرا في قيح الاسما والزاروري من الأثير لأن السبب بستجلب مقعده المنح
مقدمه موركه هلا اللت الكتيم في المتن ولامرت في المنالى من ريا
طبلا واما المته ومن ايطلب وردادو في مناض الأرض المعفنه وتحرل له
النوع والمزودخركه لطيفه لأضد من في قائد ناعمه لكثيم ما ادنه لو
يكون الاى في ارض فأبعد عنه والما الجليده وديب والكين فملطه
والجا للأكى كخوضيما المكونه الجثه ورديه بسلا دما بعد في المثنا
سبب للملوح ويولد للمكيم وينجرفه الصيف سبسل اليثم والصغنه منله
المرا وكاض فمها وإخلاط الأرضبه بها ومطال المطيف منها بول في خثانها

Left page:

الطبل وفي مليم وبجل الأسياء ميم وصف منهم الأطراف ما المنابت
الرئات ونطلب عليم يمنع الأكل والمطر فيم ويسر وثمه وريا وفعلا
فالاسبق الأجبار الملابه وام وفيعا من في زنلو لطفا ما للطلا لو ضمن
لهليم ويضعف كاما دهم ويفعل مثل لهم بسبب الطلاس ومنولد لهم الجنو
لن والجاس بل والدماك والأدواء والتخم خصوصا في المسا
ومنسه على مناهيم الحل في اللا ولا ذا دجينا لو الناحيه منه من مكث
يزمنل تها والجبل ولا كان ذلك يبكر سيبا لأفهم الأدروكا ايم الملك
ودفوح الثاني ومالاو وبعدهم ومكث بسشلرتهم والم ويكون ماذى
ومنسه الأثنا وكأنه والنوع ومنهم مليس الحقم لهيم مطلهم
المأ الا الكل كف كاس عبر معايفه الهند الذيا المبر مثل من من قبس
ومن حر الملأكثيم سسنل الأكل ماندا وميدم بيند وابواب طبيل
ماما حجم عرفان فه سفلاو لأعاله وريا يكان وفكث منه من بقره وبسم
الاسعاله الى الحسن في ايلاط يطلو واحو واصحاب الحجيات والله على عليهم
المراديل للملكيم وعثر يمه الحكايمه الى الحثر ومثل وبالله لأنضاج لأثمه
الى الطهاج والطيباه الملقيفه منهم يراه واما في المدينه والمنا والطيبا لكن
translation:
Right page:

The subtlety of water: every fine substance is receptive to actions, and when it is brought to the finest state, it is least resistant to compounds and mixtures. When the waters are stagnant and accumulating, they become a necessity of harm. A thing that is most receptive to purification from all that — when we want to refine the water for building homes and the like — is its association with substances that mix with impurities. Such refinement prevents what impedes the softening of the water through contact, as is the case with natural formation and craft. The water must be corrected, for the more abundant the water, the more it draws out the dense eighty-fold mineral content. The great benefit comes in clearing the essential cause, since the cause draws in the benefit. The introduction moves it away from the dense layers in the depths. And as for the stagnant water, it settles in the low-lying and putrid areas of the earth, thus transforming the type. The movement of light water is most opposed to what settles in the coarse, stagnant bottom. If it is in a low ground, move away from it. The cold water and its companion the dense one mix together. The heavy thick water, composed of coarse and bad sediment, grows far in the bladder. It causes the salty taste, generates turbidity, and in the summer it flows through paths of pestilence and produces corruption from it. The waters mix with the earthy components within it, and the fine quality of what passes through it as urine carries sediment within it.

Left page:

On the nature of physicians and description of their character — among them are those at the extremities in their habits. The lungs demand from them the prevention of eating and exposure to rain and dampness, cold, and effort. The most prior of the matters is clothing and water and being settled in the shade, protected from the burning sun. Their constitution weakens, and they act similarly, being caused by the expansion of the senses, producing in them mental disturbance. And the depths of the brain and the humors and the digestion, especially in the evening — among them is the state of the easy and the loose, in the region that stays for a long time. The mountain and what is present there causes, it is said, a burden on the understanding of the kings. The second exhalation and the waters and the increase of their settlement and their staying — and it becomes harmful. And the third and its companion and the type among them who wears the tightest garments for them. The water is the only vessel — like a mirror — whose reflections come from the depths of India among those. The heat of the most abundant draws the food toward it and moves it toward the gates of the body. As for the one whose constitution is hot and dry, the food and the air and what is in it from the cattle and the cattle — the cough leads to the best of what is applied, and the companions of the ailments and God upon them. The measures for the kings and the increase of their narrations toward the ripening and the digestion. And the physicians and the fine ones among them see it, and as for those in the city and the fine ones — but God knows best.

text:
الصفحة اليسرى (129b):

في بعضها نافع وفي المديد سلب عليه الأحشاء من فم الأذن
فإنها من الأقوى إبراء وسذكر ما الحال عا يجمع ما إذا بذ
للجداول المكن إذا كان خبيراً بما طلا آوردنه الماء من
خارج إذا كان الأعضاء صالح ما إبراء ملحنا والحال كلها نافلا
الأذن أكمت من سار كلما ونضج وبحر حاصب في ذاطم عاد
إلى الصلاح بلما الحجز من باب والبوركنبا في غريبه من
سافطه تالأطعان تبرج بها المابحجي يا عرجا الطبه ولا ما الدا والمصد المتشك
المفلال وقولبا لا الأصمان إذ كان يضف المصب وضراعبات أولاء
أوحشا يوما من نبه الهو ومن سطل البلدة والحا وبنفس الضمن وتطلق الطباع
فلاسكل اللطيع للجال ودماء أودى إلى الأسنفا والأذن والبلل وإبدال أذبت
فأتا الممشن فان كانت فاغل معنى كان أن كبا من ذلك فشبع على أذا أذبن
قليما ماعصل الممشك وأطلق الطيب ولكن الأسكان منه ودى وفي من
المتد ما أشبل المتيئه وبيابا لاطلق العلق والذي ماهم المال
الحاربا الصنبة المتبع الأنبوات والحكماء لا ما الأنبوان وأصحاب الصلاح
البارد واصحاب المد والذن بن من تود في الجلل والمور وأورام خلف

الصفحة اليمنى:

الأذن واصحاب الطب البوال مم فرح في الحاجبات وفي فائق
الصدد ودود الطب ما البول والمكل الأذن الملك قم منه ومثل وصف
وسهل والولا المجلا الأذيب منه بنفس ابتهل يا المجس الصنف في طبيبه
الذم قولها الحكم ويحب ما لأذون وما الأذون والحصا بالله علمنا والبده
ما دارن الطبنكون كبيراً ما بنفسه ومن بداء المثل إلى البلطه المقبل لأجيا
في بطنه فطا اتحذارنا من نبران أنا الذم وللجلاجلات والنبتا الذرى
طلول الطبيعة من شبه منه أهملجه شبه أو أحقن به والمنبه يبعر منه زبلان
فضول الطبح من بعضها للمر وسبلان الأوباس بما ولد ما اسلك اله إلى اره
للحنجة الإذا في المتسمذ لما الهلودي ريح ذلك الطالق ومن على الباه والطأء
صالح الفاد المخ الجالح فإذا الخلطب ما وخلطه له سببه ودريت الفا قلما
وبدنا أدم البلماه الفاسد في فبات المساقب وذكرا في أحكام
الماووصفا ئه ودوخى أصل صادنه في أدويه المف دكده
الفضل السابع عشر في موجبات لاحتباس المياه إخبارن
ما يجلان فزصنف به الطبر يكون أما الصنف الأول أولما الله الماء ماسكة
فقسمت به والطف صنف ما إذا الهانه من فطبول الطبيعة تيفع إلى علا ملمنا رزعا المرعى
translation:
Right page:

On the ear and its conditions: certain things are beneficial, and the prolonged use of some substances draws out matter from the ear canal. These are among the strongest remedies. We will mention what the condition requires in cases where the physician is expert in applying washes or introducing water from outside, when the organs are suitable for treatment, and all such conditions prove beneficial.

The ear, when a substance accumulates in it and matures and settles, returns to health. The barrier between the passages and the canal becomes foreign to it. The waters and the blocked passages become damaged. When the discharge and contractions occur, discomfort results and the natural functions are disrupted.

When moisture spreads to the passages and flows to the teeth, the ear, and the wetness replaces what has dried, if one finds that the matter is abundant and spreads throughout, one should soften the obstruction and free the passages. However, keeping it contained allows it to flow and the waters settle.

One should guide the body toward the treatments recommended by the physicians and the wise: treatments for cold conditions and those who suffer from prolonged illness and swellings of various kinds.

Left page:

On the ear and conditions of urinary medicine: joy in the treatments and excellence of approach. Discussion of urine and its retention — the passage of the ear is comparable in nature. One should use simple remedies suited to the physician's knowledge.

The physician should consider carefully, by his own reasoning, what is analogous to the swelling, directing it toward improvement. In the belly, one should take precautions using preparations of herbs, roots, and plants of the highlands. The natural constitution resembles these, and one may use enemas with stimulating substances to expel the waste and open the passages, treating what is retained in the throat and the digestive tract.

When food is corrupted and the humors are mixed with corrupt water and the waste remains in the passages, we mention this in the chapter on treatments of compound remedies.

Chapter Seventeen: On the causes of retention of waters.
Know that there are categories of this: the first category concerns those substances that hold water back. These are divided — one type is that which, when the nature of the body demands expulsion, it draws the matter upward and outward.

text:
الصفحة اليمنى:

الطبيعة إلى أسفل الهمزة والصول الحارك والتدد فيها والغلط المادة
اللذين كأن بريك ما لاهوي عليها اللاذمة والفقدان لأحسان المالحة
التي دفعها أن كان قد عدنبن في الأسفراع قد والذته كا يرضى في العلويز الرياحة
إذا أصراف من قع الطبيبه إلى جهبه الأخرى كا يرضى في الجبار ابن من
أحيان البولد احيا أسلام المارسب كذت الأسفل الغوارف من جهة فترى
بل ذاوف احيا سلايجل ان يسفع من ضع كل مرامض الامر بالاسفن
الاركيب قانبله والاسنعا والمسغ الملث وأسنبه ذلك والمارض من
المراض قالمسغنه وأيضا أحضان الحال الغريب والسجان الى الأبا
وابضا انطقا الجالد الغريبه من هلول الأضنان أوشده فصفه البه
وابضاغلبه التهوبه على البدت والمت لأرضال المسرك قا فاضلاع
الأذعبه وانهاأها الى المحمة من أزدياب سباب الأمراض بضها الذاوث
بنداعبا الأجياسل يأنفر من الفت الخط في الخشف عسبي مراع مع
الجنب ♦ ولتامن الأمرالغن الركبة ما الأدله والمتوار والسفراع خامجت
ان حسن يكون المه الذابقه والضفت المالسكدا ولاينا الماده بالمثل
لكنها والامتند لرضها اطواللذي لحدي فها وحوار مها أولارقه الماده

الصفحة اليسرى:

يكون كاتها سبنل من منها لفقامه منها وبين ما سعه الحارك كا يرض
من بلاللقال ومن أسفناها فما طلواك ولا سطاعها عرضا ما البا ضامها ان فيما يها
في العات والعدث شكل الأنباع بتاد سبن غناريج المخلاف لاذي لذا وارغ
اسفله ملع المعين خجبن عرض من بكث رده الملع باستفراغ المادة التي
سدى منها الحالان البض ابن يبرى منه من ناع من ماجت إذا كان ما يسفراع
أو ادا المراح من البلم أوفبا من إعداد الله مثل الفسوكن الحال والمفط
كالفست فسق وتعرض من شكل الكبالبند الماث والمالث ويا يرض منه
اليلبه الكبالناس الذي لتبه ذكريا وفي عرض الحان وذلك عند عدل
من ابن سلم اسفراع الخطا الحطف الخف ومن يفن من الحاله من حجت
والحان من مكس حال ابن الحاله من منه ما ضغا مضا يا ما يكت البلم
عريبه كان ملك الحاله ابكن عوض كل استفراع مع يبه وسطه رده
من يب جهم الأعضا من يا لانا يصنها بها انا لن يب نها ما انا ومن عيث
صاللجه وتندمس اسفراع المفت المفبه مفن ما من للمراض الله المفن
بسل المعوف ونداداما وسنه الأسن والكان الهد وسنه الحالاه يلم
المعندمن الصادنت لا ولتت صاحبه أليها الإما فيها فما ضا نت المها
translation:
RIGHT PAGE:

Nature [drives] downward the matter, and the movement and slippage of the material — those two things which are as if they have no support upon the necessary [elements], and the loss of the beneficial salts. These are expelled when [the body] has been purged downward, and the matter flows as happens in the upper [regions of the] body. When nature turns from one side to the other, as happens in [certain] conditions, one sometimes sees that the downward [evacuation] and the [bodily] passages move in one direction. Sometimes it is best to purge from all diseased [matter] by downward [evacuation]. The compound [remedy] is sufficient, and [so is] the electuary and the licking-medicine and things similar to that, and [other] diseases. The compound [remedy] is also useful for the states of abnormal temperament and for [treating] constipation toward the lower [regions]. Also, [it helps] the loosening of the skin from the dissolution of the teeth, or the intensification of their description. Also, the predominance of [bodily] agitation upon the body and the persistence of [bodily] dissolution — the rib [condition] — the organs and their contents toward the heat — from the increase of the causes of diseases, some of which are those [already] mentioned. Beginning with [the treatment of] the organs, one should take the [appropriate] line in the prescribed [manner], treating the side [condition] together [with it]. As for the management of the compound [remedy] of the knee — the proofs, the measure, and the [downward] purge — it is [most] appropriate that the quality of [the remedy] be maintained, and the dense [matter] be made like milk, and that the matter be [treated] accordingly. But [the physician] should maintain [its] condition and attend to its nature so as to direct it and keep the matter [under control].

LEFT PAGE:

[The evacuation] serves as a channel from among them to establish [the proper] level between them, and the capacity of the motion is as [required by] the illness. From the [logical] argument and from their description, it covers [the ground], and we cannot exceed what is presented to us — [namely] that among them is their mutual agreement. In [the discussion of] qualities and occurrences, the form of the types [of ailments] requires a guide leading [us] to the [appropriate] evacuation — the [downward] purging of the matter which has caused the obstruction. The two [opposite] conditions flow from it, one perceived from the other, [occurring] when purging [takes place]. Or when the remedy comes from the phlegm, or [the remedy] is prepared [from] such things as the [appropriate] laxative remedies — like the [appropriate] compound, and [similar treatments]. Such [conditions] present themselves in the form of liver [ailments] and compounds, and [ailments of] the spleen, and those who are [affected by] them. The [appropriate] remedy for [those] people, as mentioned, [is used] in [treating] the condition, and that [remedy] is applied when the slippage of the error is mild, and from what is found of the condition — from among the [medical] arguments — so that what is pressed [upon the body] is measured. When the blood ceases, [the remedy becomes] strange — it is [applied to] the whole condition, every purge being accompanied by an appropriate measure. From [within] the organs, one [can] not find what helps them unless one knows what is [needed]. And [the remedy] is applied and the [downward] purge of the compound is managed [carefully], for the purpose of the ailments and [what is] needed. [One uses] the known [remedies], and [their] continuation, and [considers] the years of age and [appropriate] quantities. Those who are [thus] treated benefit from what they are accompanied by, and what directs them [toward health] preserves [their] state.

text:
Right page:

الصبيه فقد كلمنا في الاسباب المنورية وحسنها وان كانت مما لا يكون اكثر اوجاعها ضرورية مما نأخذ في الابواب الجزئية
الفصل الرابع عشر
كلام كلي في اسباب سوء الهضم وندرته وانسانه لبكا ان فيه انه باب
المرض الضرورية ولا الانسان وهي التي تحسنها في الطبع ولا وجع ضاق
للطبع وهم مع آلامه البدن عن الهنا فانه ضرورى قبل
الاستحمامات وانواع الذك يجب ان اولد كلي فيه في هذه اسباب
فقولنا انما اسا الفاعلة في بدل الانسان حائح بالملاات به فنفعل بذلك
حمين فانها ابنفل فنه اما بعود الطفنه فيها في الما لرقوق منها فا غلبما
مانه اوقبضد للاعضا الما من هاسما اوانسانه من الاكثير ما لما ان يفعل
لا خلاطه الملاء لكثيبه سرفه حبه البدن وذلك الملانه الكثبه
ما قبل كالطلاء المبردا بنفسل فبردا الكيا والمستعملفبيل لسرع ما بالان
هاين الكيفه بالون كل الحار المريع نا جمع سما في نفا الد يحجبها
الي الفعل ما ما با نبراء الملاه من لا نبردها لنا ول
لسل فانه اذا صد مه من خارح فيتح ولامر من داخل فنقه بما
الاوضع اذا جاء نبران فانه من ربه عن بعد ما ويان طلق اولى اغظما
المكرسل الاسفنج فانه ويان ربه عن بعد ما اعظما وان طلق ايفعل

Left page:

من ذلك شيأ منهما ما فنعل من الوجهين حيفنا والبث في الفتل والسلامه

It is held among the principles that the solid organs and the heart and its approaches share a common quality — that the mixture acts upon the parts, and the nature of the humor in them works by expulsion when it is stirred up. The lower part receives the fine agents, and the dense humor is directed away. It is said that the opposing quality of cold and the demands of the flux and its counteraction are involved. When the body receives the agents and they reach the organ, the antagonists counteract it — as has been described — and the universal agent reaches downward, and the first principle is established upon it. If this is verified, then it remains effective; and if the treatment follows the mixed and the simple in every method, the result belongs to the warm and the complex.

Left page:

The substances come through simple means from the aspect of seeking them — because the cold and moist combined work in a particular way. The classification includes: what is warm-moist, what is complex in its composition, and what the simple faculties do. The pure among them, when clarified, follows its course and directs the humors as the cold agent indicates. The compound likewise, when uncovered and presented, requires that it act upon the matter. Where it is established and measured from the beginning, the faculty among the beneficial agents works and the praise is due accordingly. The origins, including stones and seeds, fall under this chapter, and the treatment follows accordingly.

translation:
Right-hand page:

Treatment of pain: If there has occurred an excessive flow from the vessel in a disordered manner in this condition, then the natural and proper medicine is to reduce what is similar to the rough discharge from it. The purpose of the pain is so that the parts in the region of the pain are separated, and the difference between them is that the pain arises from a separation of continuity rather than from a temperamental imbalance. If cold causes the pain until it becomes dry and the pain compounds, and the separation of continuity arises from cold, it will not be necessary to cool the pain further — rather it should be warmed and the cold dispersed. If the pain arises from heat, the hot blood will move toward where the pain is concentrated with warmth. If the corrupting agent of the pain is removed and the pain intensifies until it makes itself apparent, and it does not cease after the separation of continuity, then it would be as if it originated from a temperamental imbalance, with a flow affecting the source of the pain. The pain of the joints spreads; if the pain is not resolved, then the joint should be treated; and its solution and the removal of the defect and the remedy should be engaged with until the separating agent is dispersed and the pain is relieved.

Left-hand page:

Among the types of medicines used for these conditions of itching and roughness, the most specific are: the pressing, the extending, the prolonged, the compressing, the reaching-pressure drugs, which draw the substances that are necessary, and from all of these combined comes the cause of pain. The general itching is like scabies; first among them is the pain until it spreads and dries out. The delayed pain arises from a prolonged spread of the material — it is also like a crack that has no foundation, yet may have a cause in the body; and it may not spread through the body, and the analogy within the body is that whatever extends upon it, whether spreading or not spreading through the parts at the root, is like a repulsion for the material. The remedy is: if it is seen in that without a cause pointing to elevation, it occurs from a cause in the skin, and in the joint like cartilage, the dry, the rough. And from its cause, by nature, and what occurred to some of the extremities from various directions at the edges — the new pain multiplies and mixes with the extension of the origin and connects as if separated from the extremity. The pressing pain arises from what is placed upon the location, and it is as if covered with color. If it is pressed upon, the cause of the corrupting pain is the penetration of a mixed substance that separates the material and divides the skin and finds the origin of all connections to the muscle. And the cause of suppressed pain is what is found in the middle of what prevents the surrounding area from returning to the compressed state.

translation:
Right Page:

This is also specific to the genus of what generates the natural humors in the body, so that the second sensation occurs in the genus of what connects the natural members. Everything that is ingested becomes the foundation, and the sensation occurs when what is described meets something agreeable or disagreeable — then there is pleasure or harm. This is how natural preservation works: when the body is in balance, the natural constitution is maintained. The sensation of smoothness occurs when there is contact with what is compatible.

Chapter Three on Nature and Methods: How Perception and Movement Occur
Movement is attracted toward something or repelled from it, and this is called Chapter Eight.
On how perception occurs: the layers of perception are organized so as to produce sensation from them, as the drawing together of faculties constitutes perception.
Chapter Six on Methods: How perception returns, described in terms of extension and duration.
This may occur through the attraction of organs, acting through their pathways toward an intended goal within the duration, or through the layers of organs, as capacity distributes among the layers of tissues — and how the instrument works, connecting through the flesh and between the skin by means of spreading.

Left Page:

Their varieties, like the devil of the stomach's secretion, their rapid natures drawing everything inward together with what thickens or flows within them, mixing with them.

Chapter Three on Methods: Causes of Difficulty and Fatness
These arise from seeking what is not in the natural order of retention and expenditure, losing balance.

Chapter Four on Methods: Causes of Digestion and Similar Matters
This results from the material basis: food and drink together, whatever is most beneficial to the body. It is especially important to regulate meals between hard and soft foods, including meats, spongy foods, and bitter foods among edibles. Among drinks, the acidic and diuretic should be noted, along with what descends from these into the digestive organs, and the times of eating and drinking should be managed carefully.

Chapter Three on Methods: Causes and Best Types
The summer season renders the organs cold, acting upon the members and supporting the constitution. The faculty within the organs maintains stability, particularly with respect to cold treatment, since cold repels what was previously classified.

When the condition is such that vital functions are impaired, the innate heat within — since the noxious quality prevents the temperament from receiving nourishment, neither benefiting it nor corrupting its substance — repels the strange incoming heat; the spirit that sustains it is thereby diminished and drawn away, and its warmth is consumed. Among the opposing cold forces that resist through direct confrontation, and among those that guard against coldness, are those that neutralize and resist through the balance of incoming and outgoing forces. The strange vital spirit struggles to maintain the natural functions when nature is diverted from its proper course. When the inherited vital heat encounters this strange quality, and nature is occupied with it, it directs the natural faculties toward expulsion and preservation, mobilizing them to seek the proper channel of discharge. When the condition is weak, nature is impeded from performing its expulsive functions between the faculties. The strange heat then confronts portions of it, loosening and permeating them, moving them with a strange motion, so that the vital innate force — though strong — together with the coldness that is antagonistic to the yellow bile acts upon it, producing these notable strange effects.

Likewise, when things accelerate, they indicate that the mixture has shifted somewhat. When the pulse is strong and regular, it indicates a tendency in the flow of its force. As for suppressing a hot temperament, it is known that this results from the flow of the natural fluid, together with intensification, leading the vital spirit toward its natural state. Some conditions resemble the natural state — it returns entirely to the general states of the temperament — and nature drives it, so that the vital spirit guides it toward its natural goal, and what remains of it is extracted from the natural faculties in the end.

translation:
Right page:

On treating the body and the foundational principle of preventing the causes of disease: when the liver departs from what is naturally required, and if that departure is natural in the sense that the natural faculty inclines toward what is necessary, then the lesser faculty governs the constitution. The treatment is to regulate the expulsion of waste. This is because the faculties are corrupted when the balance of heat and cold departs from the natural state. This indicates that the innate faculties and the vital powers govern the body's warmth. The faculties of retention, attraction, speed of movement, the quality of speech, the management of anger, swiftness of motion, and physical capacity all depend on this. If the natural heat diminishes, one should seek to restore it with appropriate remedies. Repelling harmful influences from the body, and protecting it from injury, is essential. When one observes irregularity in urination and other excretions, this indicates an imbalance. Therefore, one should use remedies that correct and restore natural function. Cold compresses and firm treatments are among those that expel harmful matter from the body. Aloe, colocynth, and similar substances are beneficial for the intellect, comprehension, and memory. Clarity of speech, eloquence, attentiveness, and proper functioning of all the faculties depend on the balance of the humors in every case.

Left page:

On iron preparations and compounds, including astringents and those that act as constrictors: their effect is to accelerate the natural processes and restore the body's constitution. It is known that whoever is dominated by a particular humor has his constitution governed by it, while whoever maintains balance among the humors is protected and kept in health. Every mixture that corrupts a humor corrupts the whole constitution. This belongs to the chapter on the balanced and wholesome temperaments, and on the morbid and corrupted ones. When the body is overcome by harmful influences, such as animal bites, venomous creatures, convulsions, and sneezing caused by irritants, the extremities are affected in summer and autumn. The hands become weakened. In summer, natural digestion is assisted by the proper use of digestive remedies. Sneezing is induced, and compresses are applied using cooling agents. Drying and astringent substances are used to reduce moisture. The natural faculty is thus supported, its proper flow is restored, and all irregular and excessive conditions are brought under control.

The pulse has general causes whose appearance is in the function of the pulse. These general causes, after their general action, function in the necessities of the pulse. Chapter Six: On the Requirements of the Retaining Causes of Breath
When the natural force is obedient to them, the vital spirit within it responds and the nature is restored. If nature is great, it aids the faculty toward that, and if the faculty is weak, it becomes aligned with the need, so that it is not without correction alongside that. The response is then compared: the smaller [pulse] and the weak one and the small action — these are among the causes of smallness. The smallness of firmness with need makes the faculty known, with the vital spirit, for the vital force.

On the signs of milk production: The milk of a woman for her child is among the greatest and most suitable, because the need of the growing body for nourishment is met by what nature has provided, and it is appropriate and agreeable. There are many points to consider, and it has been mentioned that among the qualities are the threads and fibers of the breast, and they are like channels that help bring it forth, because speed before the child is born, and that is what regulates the state of the child — and thus it is settled. As for the moisture and softness of the breast, it relates to the ease of flow of milk, and balance is required in the temperament. For what strengthens the bodies of some children lies in the nature of their constitution, and in preventing softening. The means by which the nurse is chosen is from what is wholesome and abundant, so that the needs of the child are met. For children the gathering of fluids of digestion takes place at each feeding according to what they need, and among them is what refreshes and nourishes the humor. Milk is taken and given to the child in portions during the night and day, and the vessels absorb it. The temperament is balanced at first, and the middle of the path is the middle of nourishment, as we have said, in the balance between the extremes.

[Left page:]

Every faculty in the tongue depends on the nervous system and comes from the principles of natural law. In digestion, what appears is that it is the natural care which God has placed within it, and the complete and pure thing is what produces sufficiency and benefit. Therefore the act of nurturing the believer in the principles of growth and balance and health is related to the appropriate pleasant things, not the harmful ones. The argument of the hot temperament is most intense in what it causes in the bile and pain, and the harm is aggravated the longer it persists. If the hot temperament is of a mild kind, it is beneficial and gentle, and the subtlety of the temperament is in its place, and it produces within the soul what is praiseworthy in action. The humidity in the cavity of the womb and its surroundings and sides and what flows around is attracted to strengthen the constitution. When the heat increases and the power is purified, then the weakened constitution reaches wholeness and soundness, and balance and moderation are achieved without excess. And that by degrees — softening and moderating the hot constitution gradually, and the ultimate benefit of the hot constitution is thus established.

Weakness and wasting arise from this cause. If there is anxiety along with an acidic condition, it is sound. When the expelling faculties of the two governing principles are diminished, the roots dry out. It has been stated that when there is a deficiency arising from its companion organ, the duration of that deficiency may extend. What was intended — and the other parts — is that if the expulsion fails and the constitutional makeup is not reinforced by what is needed, then the intelligent, affectionate, and temperate nature governs, so that the dominant faculty of the body's vital constitution channels the severe movements. The seventh chapter, concerning the separation of the humors: The dominant humor settles throughout each joint, moves through its substance and its summer aspect, reaching the people of the region in a humid, temperate form, acting upon the receptive and moist faculties. Left page:

The second treatment: it is directed toward the two alternating states, to repel what weakens them, and for this reason the treatment comes to correct the imbalance. The whole constitution is reinforced by drawing it toward what is suitable and similar, which strengthens the regimen. What must be given to the body is a temperate corrective to address the weakness. As for the intermediate seasons between the main seasons, they participate in the qualities of those seasons and share in their properties. The eighth chapter, on regional climates: Regions differ in their seven qualities, and among them are those that are mixed, and among them those whose recognition determines the rules of the disease within them, as I have explained in the general chapters. The sixth chapter, on the remedies and their administration — their qualities and compositions as a basis for their qualities: If one accepts the preceding discussion of the arrangement, and if what has been sought has been settled and is sound, then the moisture of the air and its natural temperament produce differences. The scholars have been studied so that the actions of the vapors and their effects upon buildings and settlements are understood, asserting that the qualities will be governed accordingly. These fundamental causes — whether found simply in books or in complex combinations — if the dominant factor is sought and found, and if the resulting state is sound, then the outcome is well-regulated; and if mixed, then it is moderate and encompassing.

Chapter on the Pulse: As for the pulse at its peak, its characteristics vary according to the time of day. At the onset of sleep, the pulse becomes small, weak, and slow, because there is no need for the dilating forces in the vessels, nor for expansion and purification. Everything moves gently, like the stirring of chaff, toward the front. The waste products and residues are present, and conditions are not favorable for driving the humors. The body returns to a state of fullness, and the thick material within it moves slowly because the needs do not require the body to be driven. The beginning of the night, from the early hours of darkness until the first watch, is where this is known. The pulse resembles sleep in a way, as if it were the pulse of one resting. If one examines the greatness of it carefully, and studies it thoroughly, one finds in it a sign of good heat. The body's movement when a person eats should not produce in it what resembles the two types described, and they should not be found to go outside.

Left page:

The cold moves it along its continuity, including the speed of food digestion during the day. What the white produces passes through and increases in the body, just as it does in the place of generation. This is because the pulse moves outward, and the side contracts. As it increases, the body adds to itself from what surrounds it. But as it increases further and grows larger and faster, and as the humors are balanced and the conditions repeat, the pulse returns to half its strength, with the smallest of its qualities. The chapter that one should hear from both of them is what the pulse indicates when it falls at a certain point, including the purgations and the evacuations. This occurs when the day's residue diminishes, and the child of the humors — the small, slow, and variable pulse — appears. The falling pulse has characteristics of benefit: when nature drops, it is because the pulse followed it. It moves away from ignorance and error, toward what the discourse returns to as the most significant matter.

It indicates the neighbors and varies in its portion, and what their movements supply before it. For it increases and gathers, and its cutting off from what is drunk and after, from the subtleties.

[Marginal note: Al-Mudakkan]

text:
Right page:

عن سليج وكلما كان كثيفاً فانه اذا كان البول فيه ايضاً وكان أحمى
قبل الهضم ان تجا الجهة الى جميع ما يكن عسير البول ويعجل بل
لطيفات الحضن مثل البول الذي يعرض الى المقسمة والتغاير وإنما
تعرف بالتلبيس والإفاف اما التسفي فانه دل على ردى وكذلك ما أفيه
جميع الا البارد طالما فانه دل ان على جوانب سديد اللوني اسم
من البارئ والبارئ مبدل على البشر والبيسان زبل من الأول الملخص
من علي صغر ما ما الاسهال توف فانه دل على الكبد السديد في اكثر الأم
مصدر وبخضرمة وقبلاً الله فانه دل على ضرب تصويب يتجي
ان مبتسم الجسف سالجيد والتجارئ سديدة الأداء على القيطل ٥
واما طبقات اللون الاسود ما الاسراك الطبيعة قطرها ان يبقي لبنة
كان في البرهان وبل على الصف لا كاصف منها اعلى السرد الجادثه
من الصفل وبل الى البرهان أومنه اسود آمنه لقبنه وبول على أسود الآلخ
واسود آمن جنس والتلبيسة وبول على السوداء الاصرف والبول الاسود
في تجملة بول ما على شلد احلال ذا ما أطلبت بردل ما على ميتي ينن
المران البفكر فيه وما إبراء ومات علمنا وات ذو من الطبيعه الفضلات

Left page:

السوداء وهو يسبل على المكنون بأن يكون هذه ما أكثر أصل دل
سلق ويكون تقسمة ولا يكون أصفر وكثيراً ما يكون في فضه سلطاً طلب
الاسواء البضن من ذلك المجتمع المكثم وتكون شديد الشراب الى
دعاقتنوا وصفر من امعه وكان وهما كان أضعف البلال يضرب الكبد
البرهان ويسبل على المكان من أراد أن يكون تقدمه وبلى الى التلخيص ولكو
ويكونا الفضل لبيلا لا يصيا كأنه ذا يكون نجات لا مملكة وقدعرف
البال ما زياتين إذا اذا كان مع البول الاسود فأن دال على ذلك والاسود
الهوان وكان له كان جهة عدل الالهه أضعف من ذلك والا على ابرود ذه
فانه من إذا أعرض من الطبيعه وجلام مكن مكن الجهة الطالث على سبيل
السمنه والبرهان لا تكون ما في حال لا للطاحل الالطاع اجبالي الطهر
والتم والبرهان الداربات أبو البلاء السوداء و البيتله والافات فارضه من
أحباس الطب واجبار المعنا ذبل من المعقد وخصوصاً اذ اذا أغاث
الطبيعه الواو النسأء به الأداء وكما يصبل لدنا لاواق وبوهم طمم
نصل الطيعه وصله الله اوبان يكون الزعرب ولعقدمه وصنع الماي
صادفنا المدن من عقبه يكون حتما ويكون كبر المفلات نهاب ما ان ولا يكن هكلا
translation:
Right page:

Regarding the sediment: whenever it is thick, and if the urine also contains it and is very hot before digestion, it indicates that the condition tends toward all that makes urination difficult, and it hastens the fine substances of the abdomen, such as urine that leads to division and alteration. These are recognized by turbidity and opacity. As for the frothy urine, it indicates poor health, and likewise whatever is coldest for a long time indicates that on its sides there is a firm color whose name comes from the raw and the changing, which transforms the skin. The sediment from the first extract: regarding small amounts, if there is looseness, it indicates liver trouble in most cases of pain. The source and the greenish tinge before God indicates a type of correction. The good, firm, well-directed urine achieving the goal is noteworthy. As for the layers of black color, the natural dark sediment remaining like a tile deposit — in the proof it indicates the quality, the most notable of which is the hardened layer. From the extract and the proof, some of it is black, affirming the black color. Black of pure bile type and black urine in total urine, if it becomes dissolved and one seeks cold remedy for two reasons — the thinker considers it, and whatever is cured and known comes from the natural waste products.

Left page:

The black bile: it indicates what is contained within, being the most dominant element. It becomes divided and is not yellow, and often appears in a place that requires treatment of the lower abdomen from that collected and concentrated matter, and the harshness of the drink increases. It was said that whenever it is weaker, the bile strikes the liver. The proof indicates that from what was wanted, it tends toward the summary and to composition. The waste matter becomes thin and does not settle as if there is no domain, and it was known that the urine, when mixed with black urine, indicates that, and the black humiliation — if it had a direction, the divine moderates weaker than that, unless it is very cold. Then when the nature presents it, there is a way for the third aspect, the general overview of the purging. The fat and the proof do not occur in a state for the spleen except by way of the appearance of the back. The blood and the proof of the plagues, the black bile, the pestilence, and the afflictions are resistant to medical restraint, especially when the nature is agitated. The women's water indicates, as it settles, the depths and it is thought. The nature is connected, God willing, and it becomes difficult and its usefulness increases. We found in the cities from its aftermath that it must be and it grows — the large waste products — so long as it does not become thus.

text:
(Right page)
فاما البول الأسد علامة رديمة وخصوصا في الأمراض الحادة وكذلك إذا
كان عظلك طلايق فعلم من طلبه انا النطويه فاما ما الأمراض
كلها كان غلظا كان أردى وكلما كان أدرف من طاول أرآه وقل معرض
ان البول اسود أو أحمر حمد تأن يسبحه مراب الصفه
سعت فيه دلطيشة اصلاق فيخ جاله وهذا لاخطر ما دوريا كان دليل
حران صالح في الأمراض الحادة أيضا البول الليين بوله المريض
نقيفا وقته مولى في طابح يختلف فناقد كلما ما بال المطل صداع وسهر
وضم وداخلاط فعل لاسيما إذا اسبل قبلها لبلا فن زعاق نطر لب
كان ما إذا لرتبه وكان في تحيات ناثه جنس ثنه تشديد له لله اده على
السداع طالاتشال في في العفل وإذا كان عنالك سهر يسمح وخلا
عقل يصداع دلعن زعانب الدنى كل ان يكون سما التسامه في
كليه فاما دوفز البول لاسود في عالاله لتي ما البول الها فيه
مانه الاخلاط المطله وهو لبل مالك في الامران الحادة ومقول
كون البول الأسود أربا في عما العالكلي ما المتأنه إذا كان صالح فانه كل
احراف صديق فاما طب باالبول الملابات البول الأسود في المسالك لبس مساله

(Left page)
لحم ما نالم وله سوماع لا النفاد يعظم وكذلك في المتاء البول المأسوج
بعد اللعب بدلك على فيخ والجمسات في السوه في بشد الاجياث ذاك
دلذاك الليث في اسهها إذا لما تصحبه يها دلك بالا كان مين كله جيران
وإذا البول الابيض فنهد بعد ما ثقيلا فانه مع ثهمنه فضا ماسه
ذاذا انار ثانيد في ما بيسه كا بين الطاج الصافي في ما البول ايورا دالتا
ايقبرها الدال البيض المقيمه وهو المذ له دلونها الذف الترمثل
اللين والكأند وهذا المذل سافده ما اللاكون سفا ناللابيض ناللايين
للحيفه موثوه دام الالوان كله ما انا اللتهرمه ناللابيض ناللايين على البه
جملة وموثقه من التهرمه نالكون مع غلاط دال ما الملسم وإما البيض
الحقيق فلاكون الامراء الفن غلاظ في دلك كان لايان بابصده مساتها خطأ خطأ بيد
بيل على لك ثنه من ثانزم وثانزم منه بابصده يابث ومنه سمي وبلك على
دوريان الجير ومنه بيلك البول ومنه بيلك فانه بابصده ما بيابصه لبلغ ومله منب
فانم انثيم سفر ومنه فناع سباث ما بابصده ما بيابصه ما رقه وثل ميل فتح
مقصه في اللبأن البول ومن يطلب ما المتأله ما بيطلبه يبالمادة الكبير الطار
الحيد وريما كان مع حصاه البول المتأنه ومنه ماثسه المني فريما كان غرانا
translation:
(Right page)
Black urine is a bad sign, especially in acute diseases. Similarly, if it becomes very thick, the practitioner should know that this pertains to the disease's progression. In all diseases, the thicker it is, the worse it is, and the longer it takes to appear, the more concerning it becomes. If the urine is black or intensely red, one should consider the characteristics being described. If there is a drastic change in color, this is a dangerous sign indicating a serious crisis in acute diseases. Thin urine in a sick person, accompanied by headache, insomnia, distress and confusion, especially when it precedes dizziness and disorientation, is a sign of danger. If alongside this there is intensification of symptoms and headache with disturbance of reason, this indicates that there is something poisonous affecting the kidneys. As for deep black urine, it pertains to the humoral corruption in acute diseases. Black urine occurring with kidney disease, if it is moderate, is acceptable, but it is not a simple matter regarding the passages and channels.

(Left page)
As for what is known about the color of urine: the frothy or foamy urine that appears after physical exertion, bathing, and similar activities involving the body is something that should be understood. If it appears after such activities, it indicates that the body has been exerting itself. White urine that appears heavy after thinning is significant. As for urine that appears between clear and turbid — this is the intermediate type. The pale, thin, and white varieties, when mixed together, indicate a normal condition. When they combine with thickness, they indicate a certain fullness of the body. Truly clear urine is found in thin, watery conditions. Some of it settles, some is suspended, some sinks, and some mixes with what it encounters. Some of it produces sand and gravel in the bladder, and sometimes it is mixed with semen, and this may indicate the presence of stones.

text:
Right page (recto):

لا يدام ولم يتب وذهل في المخطأ أما راجع ضد من البلم التعاجم ماذا
كان البول سبما أعلى ابن على سبيل البطلان ولا الأدول ولم تنبو ولما ونع
أبدا ما نه سندبكم أو قلم وإذا كان البول اتيض فيه جميع أوقات
الحميا اصل ان يصل البلا إلى لليم البول التامون بلا ضيب ردى جل
دا الثواب في الأمراض الحاده مكث وبأص البول في لحياة أسلاحاده كف
كان البايض عندة النصغ بلث على ان للصنف ما للك عضو توركر
دا الحاله سل طلكم فيه دلت ناء هما نا لكبر الان وإذا اللكبر إذا
كان البول دما في لحياة اريض وفده دلت على تخلط العقل يكون
وإذا دار البول فيه لا لتضبه على عدل على عدم الشعر والاله
المستبه ب الباض في الحياة الحاده سندعند صيف اوعديف وانه ان مايكون
بلا أبض المزاج ماو صف ادى دولا أحوا المزاج باردة المزاج فيما فن
السفا لا كبر عن سلك البول وما سلكت به البول بلى إبض نحيب
ات بما لك البول أبض فان لوه سرفا عليه وفعله عزة أعلى فظانا وقاهه
عم هنا ذاك الملظ الملظ فاعلا في أن البائض من بردة وطلم وما أن كا ن
البلون ابش تاشرف ولا الأمثال البائض ولا المسقول والباص الحلم

Left page (verso):

قوله فاعله انه لكون الصنف دلا وإذا كان البول في المخطأ بض
لان كما دلالل السلامة مما الشمار ويجعل ما فاعلا أن المادة
الطاتها ما لك الحلي فيه الحريو الطا ولما الالا سبض المشاح وما الألله
ه كذا بلك البول في الأمراض الحاره ذا ردهه الابار اللون ضيبه انه الموا سنده
دو اللحيو بطيله الصما الأسد ل سرح في الحاوده المأرد وهما سلده ونت
عن غلبه الأبلام في الحريع العل الذي يبن المال والامباة طلبت حب المأله
الحلاها الضاب الطيبي المنا ادر مما صنيف الأمباة وترا شيب البول و
الحقيح معه كما رضاا في الحوائح المارده وما يا سند الكل وضو
في تهاعن المبتبين المابه واللركه كون في المسسفا الماوده في
امراض صيف الكبد في لا كبر مقيدان ساها اللا اللمم
الطريح وهاما السلده نجبه الأبضان الذي نجبه المبيرلون البلمر في
العرود وهنو هونة يمافه وعلمها يه البول وتعله عل
الوجه الذكر البول لأبض فان كون صينه اعم شرف نا نو الصتعلوى
كذنب سنده صينه لا كبرها وكبرلا ما كون البول الأول ول
سن كامس صلاد الطما رسب ولأرك البول في المراض وسبط ولأزكال
translation:
Right page:

It does not persist and does not return, and one errs in what returns against the phlegmatic constitution. What is it when the urine was, according to the highest authority, through the path of invalidity, and neither the first nor the second, and what prevents it always — when the urine is whitish in all the times of fever, the principle is that the white reaches the crude urine without good sign, being bad. This is beneficial in acute diseases; the urine remains and the life of the acute condition is exposed. When the whitish sediment is present, it indicates for the type that every organ is reinforced. In this condition, if it indicates that the liver is large and the large one is thus — when the urine is bloody in the acute condition, it is an unpleasant sign and indicates confusion of the mind. When the urine circulates in it without proportion, it indicates the absence of hair and similar things. The whitish in the acute hot condition, with a weak and thin constitution, and it being without whitish temperament — and the temperament is cold — then the passage of the urine and what passes through it becomes white and thin. As for the whiteness of the urine, if its color is extreme, its effect is elevated and powerful. As for the thick, the effective is that the white from its coldness and heaviness — if it is so, then the color is the most refined, and the examples of white, the polished, and the clear.

Left page:

He says: it is effective that it constitutes the type of indication, and when the urine in the error is white, because it indicates soundness, as the signs show, and it makes the matter effective. Its nature is what possesses the humor in the hot, and what the correction is — and thus is the urine in hot diseases, for it takes the appearance of yellowness, indicating that the matter is settled. The humor is tempered in what is indicated, and from the dominance of phlegm in the mixture, the one who seeks between matter and water demands the matter. The combination of the natural moisture is what the type of water shows, and the trace of urine is proportioned. Together with the cold faculties, the whole is established and in between the two motions, the matter is and the movement occurs in the acute diseases of the liver — being of the large variety, bound to the essence. The regular constitution produces the whites which generate the flowing in the veins. The veins and their moisture are with the urine and its action upon the aspect mentioned. The urine is white, for when its quality is extreme in refinement, it passes — so its quantity, large and small, is what makes the urine first. The name constitutes the settling of nutrients, sediment, and residues of the urine in diseases, settling and residues.

text:
Right page:

كان ذلك حتى يأمد في الخصم فيأمد في الصبغ والذلك طابكون بالمثباب
السمن يبض وبمن عليه صلاح الحار البن فزيي الكده يكون غير شروح
ذلك كدون لهذه الدهن والصفر والمتبن الاجن فح الامراض الحاده افضل
من الماي والأبص لقوانه ايضاً اجن من الماي والاخر الدبرى اكن
اما اذا من الاخر الصفر لوبي والاخر الصفرا وبن ايضا ليس بذلك
الخوف ان كان الصفر ايضا كأو مجوف ناكان منجركا والبولت
الاخر في امراض الكبته وذلك في الاكتب على وبم حارذ
اطيح الاس بند لجنب لطا اذا بنداالبول في الامراض الحاده الحاد
بالاحن مبغك كل ذلك ومن بيب حف منه الملاك وبرك علوديم
الكلي وان كان كلام الاحن مبن ومبى كان ذلك وبم وي في الاكد
وضعف الحالت وبيى من البول لوان الكده من كده بن ذلك
اللوز لا لسبه بسأله الطريق منهم الكده ذلك وبم دبسه دما في الما
وكيلكون من ضعف الكده وطعبكون من كمن الله وبك كن من ضعيف
الكده ما يصومت غلب وبل عله ضعفاً الخصم والملال الاعون
وان كانت لفن وفيه طيبن الامركن الله وكن المدعن وبا عنده على البلغ

Left page:

الذي ننى الفن المتبن بكاله من ذلك لو لنا الذي مصصه
فطا الطيلبه وسبه النجيح التوجه فيه بلا سفا منع وبن جسيه ذفر
من النفا لطا لطابما ما من وفي كل الامال ببل علي التراو ما وبلك عل
الحب والذهج والسلام والسلاح ونقا دا في الداو على لسن مراع ما دهم سد عل
سبل الحران منه انا يكون اذا كان يعبب به اليجه والمهلك منه ما كان
مع دسومه منا وخصوصا منا بله ما لطا ما ذا طا لطه ثن
هنا له الم قرم الطريه ذوي وهنا الكن في الاسف آو في الستل
النواجع الذوي وبقا سبل التي وبلا الوه دسما نكان علامه سلاح
حسب من بال الذي بنا في الرابر على ان المنص ضبنيه في التا
في الامراض الحاده والجاله فاذا البولا لتي بلت فا أصبات فا مذاتا
ان كون ذلك دبما اسكون اسمله منقطا ويكون علا وبلا وبا ضا فا مذا فا
لتكون سما في لونه منقطا كلي في استسل ومحصوصا فيه في قامد منقطا
افتما حجيما كا في عاله الكلي وفي كل الحال وحين من كل الارباف
وحودي ذمال الاس مزاج علب الاس علي علم الميش وفنيكون فزا الاجريرين
فمسأو دما لذلك على الاجيمات الله من كل اكن والحسان التي بنز الابلا الملذته
translation:
Right page:

When that occurs, it settles in the humor, and thereby the coloring becomes fixed, resembling certain conditions. The fat exudes and upon it rests the correction of the hot nature, so the liver becomes unobstructed. This is so for conditions involving bile and yellow humor and the mixed state — in acute diseases, water is preferable to the basic constitution, and likewise for other posterior conditions. If the yellow humor is present without great fear, and if the humor is also hollow-like and mixed, and the urine likewise, then in liver diseases this is noted as a warm sign. It is good to pay attention when urine appears in acute febrile conditions with intensity. Each of these, when its substance is diminished, leaves an impression on the kidney. If the liver's speech is moderate and the condition and flow of urine indicates the liver's weakness in this regard, then the road through the liver leads to a blood-like thick fluid. This indicates weakness of the liver; the liver fails to refine properly, and further weakness of the liver causes heaviness and lassitude overtaking the constitution. If there are good signs present and the matter is benign, then the phlegm will be well-tempered.

Left page:

That which purifies the art and establishes it through what we have said — this is what defines its character. The treatment is corrected and directed so that no harm comes, and the bodily constitution is preserved. In every matter, one must follow the principles and consider carefully what was discussed regarding treatment and the proper course. The cause of this heating occurs when something harmful and destructive mingles with it. Along with its oiliness, especially what has dissolved and softened — here the path of treatment is directed, either downward or toward resolution. The beneficial remedies and the clear signs indicate what treatment is appropriate. This is evidenced by the urine, which, when it reaches a certain state in acute and critical diseases and the urine ceases — if it was cut off and ceased to flow, and becomes interrupted in color, spotted, and especially in its sediment — then in all conditions of the kidney and in every case, one must consider all the signs. The mixture of the constitution must be treated, following the principles of the art, and one must pay attention to what the urine indicates, ensuring that the pleasant and agreeable things that flow from it are achieved.

text:
[الصفحة اليسرى - folio 180]

حسون فيه الجرم وفي الأكثر ضرع لهم أن يجتمع ذلك ومما في
الفطن وفي الكلي فعل على أسنداده لورنا فإن خص ذلك البرج م
الفعل ما جه لا يعم ذلك لا يورد ويدرك والدار بهم البدن ووجه البول
عند البراز فإن بلم منع منذ ما ذلك الملط بطلاطه ملك في
أكثر الأحوال على علم وعلم التثم وفي ملهما على خلط عليطه ها أما رد
يكون في شفح حياب يخطبه والأدوار ذلك أرم لذلك في في الأمراض
المادة يه سوء على أكثر ذلك دولار وذلك ولكن على أمله رذل بول على
مهما ما والأني سبد الغامر فيما ملك ما صتم إن ما سفالين من الغه
بالدعم يحي وبالمال على فساد المادة وكم بها ما أسباب ها جتم المحمتر
المحسب به دل على إلثر بمسهد المال الألم من الفالب بماسعبه من الراحه
وأسعبه من زيادة الضعف من البول والأسلم الخلط في الخبات باسفغ

translation:
[Left Page - folio 180]

The substance is contained therein, and in most cases it is a sign for them that these things combine, and among what is in the judgment of the kidneys, it acts according to its accumulation. For if that constellation is specified, the action does not generalize — it is not produced and not perceived — and the body's direction and the appearance of the urine at the time of defecation: if it prevents something like that, that fluid is dissipated in most conditions. Through knowledge of the sediment and in the mixture of what lies upon the humors — this is a return. It occurs in the way that the cycles of diseases cause it, the matter being of poor quality: on most of that, the circulation occurs; but it produces a heavy urine. Whatever is of a superficial kind, if the fever is present, it becomes the matter and the cause of accumulation. Through nutrition, the corruption of the matter comes about, and those are the causes of accumulation. It indicates through increase of the weakness from the urine and the sediment in the deposits. And the more the weakness increases, the urine becomes more turbid and loose, producing diarrhea. The mixing of the diarrhea combined with those dense diseases is from it, and that indicates upon the body that the digestion is the heaviest. When the turbid urine is seen, it gathers in its settling and sediment.

[Right Page]

If it is as such, and the urine darkens toward its base, it indicates a condition of difficulty.

And that is the urine.

Chapter Three: On the Matter of Urine, Its Properties and Its Turbidities

As for whether it be thick or thin — for it may be thick, or it may be distinguished without the fine part being dominant — in every state, the flow through the kidneys follows a course. The urine flows without obstruction, for the refining and processing of the sediment is the cause. The water flowing over the kidneys passes through the diseases in their condition at the risk of deficiency. When there is deficiency and increased reduction of strength, the passage of urine becomes weak and thin. The urine does not function naturally in children. Among children, the urine is naturally thicker, because children are more moist, and because their moistures are sweet and plentiful — the emerging humor's cause is their age — whatever is thin among them, in the deposits of that condition, is sharp. When one of the physicians knows of this, and recognizes it, and the urine indicates something thereby, then the physician, when he examines it, indicates a good and sound sign. When it indicates upon the liver's face and especially so, that is a sign. And this condition — if its origin is investigated — it indicates a good event has occurred.

translation:
Right page:

Among these meanings, sometimes it occurs through obstruction of the passages or bursting of the channels, so the phlegmatic humors flow. And just as it would be if the mixture were suppressed by what was indicated regarding knowledge of concoction, for concoction is the work of the natural faculties, and nature brings it as a guest from digestion toward completeness. And the strong [faculty] considers its power, and as for the total urine, it is indicative as mentioned. The nearness of the phlegmatic mixture and the dispersed [humor], and the dispersed [matter], when fully mixed, becomes complete. Half [of it] arises from the source, established therein, well-disposed, its nature being thus. When it increases, it was added, like the waters that are slow in digestion, as exemplified in this place — for weakening of digestion and weakening indicate a condition where, if it cannot rise from the mixtures, it will not be corrected, and this is so that what is in the greenish urine may be corrected. The observation is that when the bile flows and passes through it, mixing from it is not possible, but the first step of digestion of the humors is diminished, and what is correct from it appears in the color of the urine. For if the yellow increases in the depth of the patient, it indicates excessive bile. And when it increases and spreads, its portions intermix, and the condition becomes disturbed as is known.

Left page:

As for the saline [quality], and perhaps the meaning of the phlegmatic mixture and the humors in diseases is overall in three aspects: the flux occurs in a manner that what was gathered becomes firm and thick. And the formation of urine without its proper qualities, mixed with something dominant over it, so when the humors are mixed in it, it causes the appearance of clearness mixed with turbidity, and perhaps the natural mixing affects the humor. It is observed or perceived from it, but it is not digestible in the manner of natural temperament. It may indicate abundance of the organs, and as for the thick urine, from the thick [humors] comes the mixture settled therein. And the reason for that is that nature works upon the matter and digests it, and the greater the clarity the more it indicates that [nature] has striven in expelling it and completing the condition of purification from the illness. And when these two things persist and the nature maintains them and the faculty purifies, it means that digestion proceeds and as the faculty manages the matter, the observation of the urine indicates it. And regarding the narrow passages when the observation is established, the urine indicates it. And upon its qualities and characteristics the humors move and flow from the passages. And regarding the amber[-colored urine] in all the times: sometimes thick and sometimes leading to the loss of the natural faculty. And as for the urine of that kind, as will be explained.

translation:
Right page:

Know that what the thick urine absorbs altogether is best for large wounds, especially for the origin of the matter. And for this reason the heart recovers, and with hunger Muhammad saw it, and if it became mixed, it took by raising the plaster of the deep tissue with its surroundings. So the king of Thamud and Darya was following the liver. The liver, the great one, the cardiac organ, came with the dense thick matter remaining. That which was in the subtle heart diminished in weakness and became slow; what facilitated it was that this is what we contemplate: it comes from the sharp substances, and from the diseases of the smooth kind, or if it were that Islam came from a manifest disease. This is near to the urine — the natural urine — when it falls into the thick sticky matters sometimes. Over its depth, it diminishes the coarse nutrition and its quality facilitates the sound and its echoing. Sometimes it is obligatory on the collection because it indicates that the humors are weak in the vessels, and upon it is the treatment of the wound. One takes the thick heavy urine which was made — because the rejection of the long things and the mixed substances has no garlic in it for inquiry — since the quality attaches to the urine stored in the body, relying upon the humors together with the burning of the nature. And what rectifies it is the urine of the quality of the one who has released wind upon it. And the quality of the urine indicates the deficiency of the organs and their regulation, attached to it in mixture.

Left page:

As for its description: as for what the thick urine indicates — it indicates the pressure, and that is what the organ does, the smoothing and the passage. The detailed one with its treatment and what is good for it, and the indication like that, what it is connected to — upon it is born, sometimes of a sword-like nature: so it would be if it were a sign of irrigation and heat and direction in the joints and the kidneys and the liver, and the passage of the obstruction — such is the decline. From the neighbors, and if there was weakness, and if there was something resembling what is upon the path, from this — the whole for the discharge of what benefits it — if the condition is in origin, seeking the beneficial. One moves and goes to the basis: the liver takes what the thick matter supports, it was found good and sometimes by the regulation — the mixed treatment that is steady, the useful, the flowing into the liver, and the liver's nature was fine with it — it does not spread its substance and does not inflate its matter and its being. This thickness is something that when it is something from the far ones, its nature is mixed together in the faces of the treatment — that mixture. The mixture tends toward blackening, and from its number and its internal aspect the appearance of the oppressive images of the one who faces it. And upon this — those two, if it was and its description and the smoothing and the higher from the faces of the forms and the faces of the formed ones. But that is formed from the liver, gathered together, and the liver has seen the urine of the liver, and thus what came of the mixture.

translation:
Right Page:

On the falling of vital force: When the vital force weakens, cold rapidly seizes the body and urine is expelled. Similarly, what resembles the color of wind, and retention occurs among those prone to it. Among those afflicted with cold, some avoid urinating because the urine resembles lime water or the urine of livestock. It intensifies with the rising of humors and when the body's mixture is disrupted, one is treated with hot remedies. That which leaves a thick trace indicates all of this. It has been established that in those who anoint themselves, if they persist in doing so, the urine takes on the color of a certain organ, and if this persists it indicates suppression. Some among them say that if there is sediment at the bottom of the urine resembling pitch and smoke, the course will be long. If the sediment in the urine resembles small coins, the end of the period approaches with a fatal outcome. Urine with varying components, if the large components indicate that nature is carrying heavier matter, digestion is more vigorous and thorough, and urine in which thread-like substances appear mixed together, some smaller than others, indicates a gradual progression of the condition.

A comprehensive chapter on the signs from wind, the granules, and urine: It is said that urine which is excessively thin in consistency and color indicates a poor constitution and an increase in disease.

Left Page:

Regarding acute conditions, as we have previously explained: if the signs have persisted for a long time and there are indicators pointing to them, the cause lies in the disorder of urine, and this is related to the direction of the condition, in that it supports the body. If this appears in the extreme states of the matter, and urine cannot be aided, it indicates that the passages are obstructed in a strange manner. If the matter had been subdued, death approaches, as the matter of elasticity is consumed. It has been established that urine which follows the natural course, when the secondary stage reaches its peak, then God and those who are prevented have blocked it and directed their need toward a good outcome. The urine of the healthy when they persist in physical activity — in acute diseases, if urine approaches the color of what has been described, and this represents a transition, and if the surface of the urine is reddish, this indicates imminent destruction and falling of vital force.

Chapter on the most critical signs:

Recurrence of the worm-like substance that descends in the water, along with its thread and the mixing and processing with urine, and its various appearances passing with urine — if these predominate in the water, this indicates corruption of the body's origins and diseases.

translation:
Right page:

On the signs indicated by urine: when urine appears pale and clear, it is a sign of good constitution in cases of migraine. If it appears turbid, that indicates irritation and disturbance near the surface. 

Chapter Eight: On the first urines and their indications — the quantity of urine and its qualities.

It is necessary to examine the pure urine carefully, especially regarding intestinal looseness in the lower regions. The dominant and compounding elements point to the melting of vapors and the spread of superfluities. These are signs of the state of the humors in the urine concerning the condition. If the urine is thin and clear, it indicates recovery and safety. If it is mixed and moderate, it indicates an intermediary state. If it is large in volume and turbid, it is a sign of dispersion. The thin, delicate urine with a reddish hue indicates a complex condition. When the urine appears suppressed and does not flow freely, it indicates danger. The appearance of urine in acute diseases that is followed by comfort is a good sign. Likewise, the urine which flows consistently in acute diseases indicates resolution. There are properties of urine that indicate corruption and disorder in nature.

Left page:

On the benefits of examining the rose-water and what it indicates: this corresponds to what has been mentioned about examining the urine in the chapter on examining fevers and their types — especially when there is a connection to digestion and the humors. 

Chapter Eight: On Good Urine

The moderate and balanced urine indicates health and proper function of the dominant faculty. If the urine contains half its components from fine and pure elements, that is praiseworthy. It becomes beneficial and corrective when it indicates that the illness is resolving favorably.

Chapter Seven: On the Urines of the Teeth — and their effects on children

This relates to the formation of secretions and their pathways in the body. Among the young, saliva is thick, and when mixed with other substances and secretions, it indicates a certain condition. Among the elderly and mature individuals, the secretion becomes thinner, and when it is moderate and its excess is mild, it is considered favorable. If it is persistent and heavy, the physicians have noted that this requires attention.

Chapter Ten: On the Urines of the Young, the Adolescent, and the Mature — and the general rules applying to each.

On the matter of error and the weakening of the vital faculties: the condition is indicated when the natural powers are diminished, and the resemblance between similar cases is lost among those who follow the principles. When this is established, the abundance of the condition is noted, and it occurs in the lower faculties. Upon the foundation of what is established, it is noted that the superior faculties fail, and among the causes found in the evidence is that the upper part becomes diminished. The intermediate and lower parts become affected, and when such a case presents itself, the secretions are disturbed. When the vital faculties decline, the condition worsens.

Chapter Thirteen: On the First Responses and Primary Cases.
Sometimes a physician, upon encountering a case, finds that when it is said that the matter belongs to the skin, it will be in the natural course of things — like a severe poison, dark and confused in its outcomes, resembling falsehood in its nature, though its substance remains.

Chapter Thirteen: On the Foundations.
Regarding the primary classification: the collection of essential matters from the fundamentals and their signs. When the condition progresses and the excretions increase in quality, and the natural balance between the upper and lower faculties is maintained in the proper measure — then the treatment follows the primary principles accordingly.

Chapter Thirteen: On the Countries and Regions.
The regions are established by what surrounds them, and what is known of their mixtures and compositions — from their affairs, their constitutions, and their remedies. The weakness of the faculty and the decline of its force is noted from this, and what is prescribed for the cities and regions must follow the best medical guidance presented here.

Concerning the human body at that point — when there is a mixed and corrupt humor, this leads to greediness, and that is because it corrupts and misleads, and it draws upon the heart excessively and without balance. This occurs during the process of digestion. As for what is produced from it, it indicates a deficiency between the emerging heat and the body's capacity for digestion. As for what is beyond the body itself, it has been established concerning impure mixtures and what arises at the extremities, or concerning what is settled in the moist joints — when it mixes with the original dry elements it becomes moist.

This indicates that the faculty endures in beneficial matters, and there appears from it a degree of moisture and density. When it is associated with all erroneous mixtures, it indicates medical signs in the matter, because of what has affected the liver in the blood and in the fluid. There are two types of mixtures — one is dominant and settled — indicating what is opposed in the body and concerning the natural color of the regions.

When this is observed, it indicates that there is an excess of black bile. If it appears pale mixed with whiteness, this indicates a phlegmatic humor. As for the correct diagnosis — it is a reliable sign — and one must take note of this and consider it carefully, to make a sound judgment.

[Left page]

This chapter concerns the indicators found in the urine, as we have sought to explain in the section on urine. Know that colors, when they appear in the bodies like darkness, indicate diseases affecting the nutritive faculty. Frequent occurrence of dark color upon the urine indicates toward the liver and its state. The blackness indicates dominance of the melancholic humor.

Those in whom the black bile is dominant — it is likely to settle in the body over time. The diminishing and transformation of the natural state indicates that the black bile is increasing and accumulating. Its expulsion — likewise the expulsion from the solid organs of a dark substance — when it exits with slipperiness and looseness, and the dark elements settle, this too is found in bodies also during growth.

As for the hemorrhoidal discharge, similarly, if it is confirmed that the original matter is expelling and directing itself, this indicates a weakness of the faculty and a weakness of strength, meaning that the expulsion of this matter and the weakening of the power indicates a weakness.

translation:
Right Page:

Concerning some of the requirements for what is suitable to take for the chest and its conditions: one should use boiled vinegar mixed with water, and likewise senna is beneficial for the liver and intoxicants. The milk that is produced by the wet nurse should be of moderate quality. The nurse's milk should be examined and taken according to what the physician prescribes. If the milk is to be given, it should be of good quality and the nurse should be healthy. It is recommended that the nurse not be too thin nor too fat, and that she avoid harmful foods. The physician should monitor the nurse's condition and ensure the child receives proper nourishment. As for the infant, care must be taken in all aspects of nursing, especially in the early stages of nursing, for the milk must be sound and pure. One should not force the child to nurse beyond its capacity, and the milk should not be left to spoil.

Left Page:

It is required that when the milk is plentiful, it should not all be given at once. For nursing, the milk should be offered gradually, allowing the child to nurse in a warm and comfortable environment. If this is not possible, a substitute may be found. The breast should be offered to the child regularly, following the first feeding after birth. As has been mentioned, the nursing position is important, and the child should be held properly during feeding. When there is a necessity to supplement feeding, this should be done carefully. If the breast becomes engorged or painful, treatment should be applied. The nurse should be of sound health, and when the child is weaned, this should be done gradually. One should consider what is given to the child after weaning and ensure it is appropriate. The child's diet should be monitored carefully, and any problems with digestion should be addressed. Milk mixed with water or other suitable liquids may be given as appropriate, taking care not to harm the child's stomach.

CHAPTER THREE: On the Diseases That Affect Infants and Their Treatment

The sick infant in treatment requires that the physician observe the child's condition carefully. When an illness occurs, it is necessary to clear the child of harmful humors, removing them gently. One should aim to purify the body gently, using mild remedies suitable for the child's delicate nature, correcting the constitution carefully, administering treatments gradually and with moderation. If a laxative is given, it should be mild and well-suited, and delivered in a form appropriate to the child's age and condition.

translation:
Right page:

Concerning the use of various medicinal compounds and preparations including theriac and other remedies: One takes the ingredients and combines them — mixing them together — with the milk of the child [i.e., nursing mother's milk] and other substances. If one wishes to use them for children, they are ground and mixed, and the compound is given. The preparation strengthens the stomach and benefits digestion. It has been said that Abu Ali [Ibn Sina] mentioned that the amount used should facilitate digestion, and should benefit the throat and esophagus. Likewise it connects and preserves the natural temperament of the milk.

Left page:

With regard to compound remedies resembling theriac in their benefit, used for treating poisoning and general ailments: these are the electuaries [ma'juns] composed of roots and used for diseases of children, and they have been recorded as beneficial. They include ingredients such as the wild plants, oak gall, dried fruits, and similar substances — these are ground together and combined. A portion of several dirhams is taken; it is mixed with fresh milk and given to the child warm in the stomach. These remedies have been confirmed to benefit those who use them. They drive out harmful matter formed in the stomach of children, and they expel superfluities. Their warming and strengthening properties come from ingredients including: cinnamon, pepper, henbane, and similar spices mixed with honey and wormwood, along with colocynth and other such things as are known in this category.
